description: One entry's archive: its receipt (what the server attests it took in), repo and commit, scores per phase with the replay's guardrails and cost sensitivity, every grading run (with its failure-draw key once published), what building it cost per model, the authorship ledger's totals (lines written by transcript turns, dead spend), what the caller may open of it (access: its transcripts are true only for its owner and admins, the deadline passed or not; to an admin's API key a rival's are false until its deadline) and its downloads. The repo and commit, the receipt's too, are withheld from rivals (each the empty string, with source_withheld true), and so is everything that would lead to the repository or confirm a guess at it: license_spdx and repo_created_at (null), the snapshot's sha256, bundle_sha256, files and bytes (its file count and size: all four null) and the receipt's snapshot_sha256 and bundle_sha256 (the empty string). An entry's source and code are its owner's and admins' only: they stay withheld from everyone else after the deadline too, its competition's winner's included. Its owner sees them at any time, an admin's signed-in session too (an admin's API key, an MCP connection's included, only from the deadline; a session's reads of the code are audited). How to get its graded code with git rides with them: clone_url (`git clone` it: <clone host>/s/<id>.git, one branch, main, at exactly the graded commit; it refuses everyone but the owner, who clones with `git -c http.extraHeader="x-api-key: af_..." clone <clone_url>`, and an admin's signed-in session (an admin's API key too, from the deadline); before the deadline git prints `remote error: sealed until <deadline>`, and on a competition with a running phase, until its results are published at the replay's end, a time not known before, `remote error: sealed until its competition's results are published`), served_by (mirror: clone clone_url; origin: the server points the entry at its GitHub repository, so clone origin_url and check out commit_sha) and origin_url (the GitHub repository it came from, which may have changed since; null for an uploaded bundle); while withheld clone_url is the empty string and served_by and origin_url null. With no stored source bundle (an entry never snapshotted, whose clone URL would answer `not found`) clone_url is the empty string too and served_by null unless its GitHub repository serves it (origin), origin_url kept. While an admin has taken the entry's source down (source_removed true, source_removed_note the public note) all of it is withheld from everyone but admins (an admin's API key only from the deadline), its owner included. Its total build cost (cost.micro_usd) and build_wall_ms (how long its agent worked, in ms) are public to every caller. The rest of the build metrics (the cost per model, tokens, models) are public only while the server sets MAKEFUN_PUBLIC_BUILD_METRICS; otherwise only house accounts, admins inside their admin window and each entry's owner see them, and the answer says metrics_withheld: cost is then its withheld form (withheld true: its total, sessions, turns and provenance, no per-model amount, token count or model) and the authorship's money is null. On a bounty whose rules name a play link (harness.entry_link) the entry carries entry_link_url (its Roblox experience's or pump.fun coin's page, its post's on X or Reddit, its video's on YouTube or TikTok, its make.fun bounty's page (https://make.fun/bounty/<slug>) where the entry names one bounty, or, on a self-hosted site link (platform site), the site's own address once make.fun read it live; make.fun never sees a self-hosted site's traffic, so no traffic figure rides it) and entry_link_image (the experience's own thumbnail or icon as make.fun's WebP rendition, GET /api/submissions/:id/play.webp: url, preview_url, width, height, kind thumbnail or icon, sha256), both only where its judged artifact shows to you, else null, the picture null too where none is kept; on a bounty whose play link is a video on YouTube the entry carries entry_link_title too (the video's title as YouTube answered it, under the same gate, null where it is null or no title was read; on an X bounty whose entry link names counts, the post's text as X answered it, cut to its first 200 characters, the last an ellipsis where it ran longer; on a TikTok bounty whose entry link names counts, the video's caption as TikTok answered it, cut the same way; on a make.fun bounty whose entry link names counts, the bounty's title as make.fun's records held it, cut the same way, where the entry names one bounty; absent on every other bounty); a hosted competition's entries carry entry_link_url alone (their hosted game). Where that play link also names engagement (harness.entry_link.engagement) the entry carries entry_link_engagement too: the linked post's public totals (likes, replies, reposts, quotes, views; a Reddit post's upvotes and comments; a YouTube video's views, likes and comments; a TikTok video's views, likes, comments, shares and saves) read when it was checked (intake) and once after the deadline (deadline), under the same gate as entry_link_url, null where it is null or nothing was read; display only, never scored, ranked or a tie-break, save on a YouTube bounty whose entry link names counts, where the video's views rank, and on an X bounty whose entry link names counts, where the post's views and interactions rank as its rules weigh them, and on a TikTok bounty whose entry link names counts, where the video's views, likes, comments, shares and saves rank the same way (views alone where they name no weights; a post or video gone scores 0): the dev board on the open dev window's newest reading (latest, else intake), the final on the reading at the final phase's lock (deadline). On such a bounty (YouTube, X or TikTok naming counts), and on a make.fun bounty naming counts, the entry's archive carries entry_link_ranked: true. On a make.fun bounty whose entry link names counts every entry carries entry_link_bounties too, under the same gate as entry_link_url (null where it is null): every bounty the entry names, in its file's order, each its url (https://make.fun/bounty/<slug>) and title (as entry_link_title is cut; null where none was read); no figure rides it, since the bounties' counted entrants, paid entry fees and pots show only as the entry's scored columns (the totals over the bounties that count), the dev board on the newest reading, the final on the reading at the final phase's lock. On a bounty with no judge whose play link is a video on YouTube, an X post naming counts, a TikTok video naming counts or a make.fun bounty naming counts, entry_link_url, entry_link_title, entry_link_engagement and entry_link_bounties follow no judged artifact: they show for a public entry of a public competition that is no house entry and whose source stands, in any phase (entry_link_image keeps the judged gate). On a competition make.fun hosts (a bundle naming harness.hosting, or a best X game contest, hosted on makefun.gg whether or not its bundle names the key; get_competition's hosting says it: a passing entrant's entry at https://<prefix>-<8 hex>.<zone>/, the zone makefun.gg or makefun.sh, only while it holds one of the board's top places: make.fun hosts only each board's top places (its hosting scope, an admin setting: the top 10 unless an admin sets another number, from 1 to 10, or every site): an entrant's site is up only while its entry holds one of those places and comes down once it drops out, whatever the bundle's harness.hosting names (every entrant, or its own top). The number in force is the competition's hosting.top (hosting.entries then 'top'), and its rulesNote carries a dated line where it hosts fewer sites than the rules name; the final's winners on makefun.gg and a superbot.sh site are never cut, and judging, ranking, the screenshots and the Feed do not change), the entry's owner and admins read hosted_site: the entrant's site (url, zone, status, held_reason, notes from the pre-publish scan, published_at, submission_id, the entry it carries now, and hosted_top, how many of the board's top places are hosted, present only while that is fewer sites than the rules name), whether or not this entry is the one it carries, as soon as the row exists, live or not, null while there is none; no one else gets the key. Where its hosting counts traffic the entry carries site_traffic: the site's views, visitor_days, the declared event's visitor_days, excluded_share, the counting window and final, under the same gate as entry_link_url, null where it is null or no site carries the entry; display only, never scored, ranked, a gate or a tie-break. To its own entrant alone, while grading runs behind for the unfinished entry, the answer carries notice (kind grading_backlog; message, poll_after_seconds): the entry is received and still processing, no action is needed and it is not to be submitted again; read it again after poll_after_seconds (300: 5 minutes). It names no place in line, count or time. An entry's code (its snapshot tree and blame) is its owner's and admins' only, the deadline passed or not, except that make.fun may publish the first-place entry's code, its result and how to reproduce it, under the entry's own licence and credited to its entrant's handle, only for a contest make.fun names for it, one contest at a time, and only once that entry's reward is paid. Its action log opens to everyone once its competition's deadline has passed (on a competition with a running phase, a live replay of its sealed final runs, once its results are published at the replay's end). Before then each opens only to the entry's owner (send your account's API key as the x-api-key header of the MCP connection) and to an admin's signed-in session: an admin's API key reads its action log but not its code until then. A closed part answers 403: before the deadline with the date its action log opens (none yet while a running phase's results are not out), after it, for a rival's code, with no date. Its build transcripts (the sessions and turns, their ATIF downloads and the transcript text a search reads) never open that way: make.fun does not publish them, not at the deadline and not for the winners, so only the entry's owner and admins read them, and everyone else gets 403 with no date. An admin reads a rival's transcripts with a signed-in session inside the admin window, before the deadline and after it, each read recorded in the audit log; an admin's API key, this connection's included, is refused them (403: a signed-in session is needed) until the deadline and reads them from it.

entry_link_image.description: The play link's picture (make.fun's rendition of the Roblox experience's thumbnail or icon), where entry_link_url shows; null where it is null or none is kept; absent on a bounty naming no play link

entry_link_ranked.description: true on a bounty whose entry link names counts (a YouTube video's or an X post's), or a TikTok video's: it ranks the entry on the counts make.fun read of its post (entry_link_engagement), not on a judge; and on a make.fun bounty's naming counts, ranked on its scored columns, the totals over the bounties it names that count (entry_link_bounties); a fact of the bounty, whoever asks; absent on every other bounty

entry_link_title.description: The linked video's title as YouTube answered it, on a bounty whose entry link is a YouTube video, or the post's text as X answered it (its first 200 characters, the last an ellipsis where it ran longer), on a bounty whose entry link is an X post naming counts, or the video's caption as TikTok answered it (cut the same way), on a bounty whose entry link is a TikTok video naming counts, or the bounty's title as make.fun's records held it (cut the same way), on a bounty whose entry link is a make.fun bounty naming counts where the entry names one bounty, where entry_link_url shows; null where it is null or nothing was read; absent on every other bounty

entry_link_url.description: The entry's play link (its Roblox experience's or pump.fun coin's page, its post's on X or Reddit, its video's on YouTube or TikTok, its make.fun bounty's page where it names one bounty, a self-hosted site's own address once make.fun read it live, or its hosted game), where its judged artifact shows to you; null otherwise; absent on a bounty naming no play link and not hosted

guide_repo_url.description: The entry's public repository page on GitHub (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>, never a clone URL, a tree or a commit), present only on a referral/v1 guide bounty's entries: a referral/v1 guide entry's public repository page (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>, its guide_repo_url) shows to everyone from the entry's acceptance, on its leaderboard row, its Feed post and its entry page; its commit, its clone and its code stay its owner's and admins' only. Null while the gate is closed (a refused, disqualified, internal, house or taken-down entry); absent on every other bounty. It is not the entry's source: repo_url, commit_sha and source_withheld are unchanged by it

held_reason.description: While held: scan:<rule> (the pre-publish scan refused its files), defender:<flag>, report:auto (trusted site reports) or admin (a takedown); null otherwise

hosted_top.description: While make.fun hosts fewer of the competition's sites than its rules name (its hosting scope, an admin setting: only each board's top places), how many of the board's top places are hosted: the site is up only while its entry holds one of them and comes down once it drops out. Absent where every site the rules name is hosted, on a superbot.sh site, and from a server older than the field

notes.description: What the pre-publish scan noted without refusing (a file left out for its extension, an eval, an absolute URL); empty when not scanned

published_at.description: When the version served now first answered (ISO 8601); null while none is served

status.description: held: nothing is published for it (held_reason says why); a hold never touches grading

submission_id.description: The entry the site carries now: this one, or the entrant's newer passing entry

url.description: The site's address, https://<slug>.<zone>/ (the bundle's zone, makefun.gg or makefun.sh; superbot.sh on a registry competition), known as soon as the row exists; it serves only once status is live

hosted_site.description: To the entry's owner and admins alone, on a hosted competition: the entrant's site (url, zone, status, held_reason, notes, published_at, submission_id), whether or not this entry is the one it carries, as soon as the row exists, live or not; null while there is none; absent for anyone else and on a competition make.fun does not host

metrics_withheld.description: The entry's cost per model, tokens and models are withheld from this caller (cost is its withheld form, its total kept)

notice.description: Present to its own entrant while grading runs behind for this unfinished entry: it is still processing, no action is needed, do not resubmit; read it again after poll_after_seconds. Absent otherwise

origin_url.description: The GitHub repository the entry came from, which may have changed since; null for an uploaded bundle, a local repository, and while source_withheld

repo_url.description: The entry's repository; the empty string while source_withheld

served_by.description: mirror: clone clone_url; origin: the server points the entry at its GitHub repository, so clone origin_url and check out commit_sha; null while source_withheld, and in mirror mode while no source bundle is stored

event.description: The bundle's declared event (harness.hosting.traffic.event) and the counted visitor-days that sent it (navigator.sendBeacon('/_mf/e', name)) after a view that day; null where it declares none

excluded_share.description: The share of visitor-days on datacenter networks, 0 to 1

final.description: True once the window is closed and counted: the figures never change again

views.description: The weighted page views over the window

visitor_days.description: Each UTC day's distinct visitors, datacenter networks left out, at most 3 a network and 50 an AS number, summed over the window

site_traffic.description: The traffic of the make.fun-hosted site (makefun.gg or makefun.sh) carrying this entry now (views, visitor_days, the declared event's visitor_days, excluded_share, window, final): display only, never scored, ranked, a gate or a tie-break; where entry_link_url shows, null where it is null or no site carries the entry; absent on a competition whose hosting counts no traffic
